title: KCSE Examination Registration
description: Draft public-service guidance; review questions must be resolved before publication.
clarifying_questions: Which candidate type, programme or assessment pathway?

claims.text: The 2026 circular set registration for 16 February to 31 March 2026. This historical window must not be presented as currently open.
Heads of institutions register school candidates online using centre credentials. Candidates should verify their recorded particulars and subjects.
For 2026 KCSE, private candidates register through the Sub-County Director of Education office.
Special-needs registration requires the prescribed form and supporting medical and assessment evidence; institutions document relevant interventions.
The circular lists repeaters, non-citizens and private candidates as exceptions to government fee payment, with KES 7,200 payable through eCitizen.
The private-candidate annex requires identity evidence: national ID, passport or alien card; where unavailable, a birth certificate and evidence of an ID application are required.
Private candidates require confirmation from the SCDE or head of the approved centre where practical papers will be taken.

Partial repeaters take one to six previously attempted subjects still offered in the current curriculum. They cannot introduce new subjects; the supplementary slip does not change the earlier mean grade.
Repeating for a mean grade requires the entire examination with seven to nine subjects, subject to the prescribed subject combinations.
The private-candidate annex states that examination withdrawal does not entitle the candidate to a refund.

The special-needs annex asks the institution for headteacher and medical reports identifying assistance. For the listed physical, mental and psychomotor categories it specifies a recent detailed medical report, EARC assessment and a full-size photograph for physical disability. Low-vision candidates also need a medical report.

citations.locator: PDF p14, special-needs form notes ii-iv

claims.text: The main circular mentions a late-registration penalty, while the private-candidate annex says entries after 31 March 2026 will not be accepted regardless of payment date. Do not promise a late-entry route.

citations.locator: PDF p6 section 9 and p10 annex section 7

unresolved_questions: Clarify main-circular versus private-annex late-entry and amendment rules for the relevant candidate type.
Confirm practical venue with SCDE; annex references to an approved practical centre and county headquarters must not be treated as a personal venue assignment.
Check subsequent amendments and obtain named content approval before publication.
